To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
galanin immunoneurons are found in laminae I and III of the rat spinal cord, and are GABAergic, but not glycineergic.
galanin immunoneurons are mainly contained in the GABAergic neurons of the superficial dorsal horn.

(1) galanin is found in a subpopulation of GABAergic neurons; (2) these GABAergic neurons are located in laminae I and III; (3) they are not glycine-immunopositive; and (4) galanin immunopositive neurons in the superficial dorsal horn are probably inhibitory interneurones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of galanin-like immunoreactivity (Gal-LI) in the rat spinal cord.
the role of galanin in the spinal cord.
the distribution of galanin in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
galanin-containing neurons in laminae III-III of the dorsal horn are GABAergic, and that most (if not all) of them are also enkephalinergic.
galanin-containing neurons are GABAergic, but not glycinergic, and are therefore probably inhibitory.

galanin-containing neurons in the spinal dorsal horn are inhibitory interneurones that are GABAergic and probably also contain neuropeptide Y, and that they do not use glycic acid as a co-transmitted inhibitory transmitter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
galanin-containing neurons in laminae II and III of the spinal dorsal horn are mainly GABAergic, and that they are probably inhibitory in function.
galanin, enkephalin and neuropeptide Y, but not thyrotropin releasing hormone, are contained in GABA-immunopositive but glycine-negative neurons in laminae II and III of the rat spinal cord.

galanin and GABA are co-localized in a population of neurons in the superficial dorsal horn, while galanin and glycine are not.
